name: Bonus
authority: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule: a bonus is an Additional Wage, charged under the Additional Wage ceiling (102,000 less the year’s Ordinary Wages subject to CPF).

name: Salary in lieu of notice
authority: https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary; https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/termination-of-employment/termination-with-notice; Employment Act 1968 ss.10,11,23(3); https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/part-time-employment/public-holidays: actual dated required work and gross contractual rates price unserved notice; written mutual waiver reduces only its covered dates. Employer notice compensation remains taxable and counts toward SDL; CPF and self-help treatment preserved.

name: Retrenchment benefit
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.45: no employee with under 2 years’ continuous service is entitled to a retrenchment benefit, and no provision fixes a quantum for longer service; a contractual or negotiated retrenchment benefit is raised by HR with the amount. CPF Board (“Are CPF contributions payable on redundancy payment?”): “CPF contributions are not payable on termination benefits given for retrenchment or loss of employment”, so it is outside CPF and, following the CPF base, outside CDAC, ECF and SINDA; Muis, MBMF employer information, Table 2: retrenchment pay — Accounted for MBMF: No. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 s.2 (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026): “wages” means “the remuneration in money, including any bonus, due or granted to a person in respect of the person’s employment but does not include such payments as the Minister may, by notification in the Gazette, specify”; the only notified exclusion is medical, dental and TCM reimbursement (S 375/2023), and no SDL or Agency publication addresses retrenchment pay. Source interpretation: law silent on this payment; default counts toward SDL, read as SALARY_IN_LIEU_OF_NOTICE is (the same s.2 words); lawful because SDL is employer-borne, s.3(2) caps it at 0.25% of $4,500 a month, and any excess is refundable under SDL Regulations reg.13, whereas the other reading risks an Agency assessment for unpaid levy. IRAS: compensation for loss of employment is not taxable and is reported apart from gratuity, notice pay and ex-gratia (Form IR8A item d3, Explanatory Notes YA 2027).

name: Damage or loss recovery
authority: EA s.29 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: one-time recovery only after an inquiry and an opportunity to explain; input amount must be the evidenced actual loss attributable to the employee. Payroll enforces the independent quarter-month salary limit. Do not split one loss into repeated requests.

name: Accommodation recovery
authority: EA s.30 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: input amount must not exceed the value of accommodation supplied and accepted by the employee; retain acceptance and valuation evidence. Payroll caps accommodation plus amenities/services at a quarter of salary for the salary period.

name: Amenities or services recovery
authority: EA s.30 and MOM salary-deductions guidance: input amount must not exceed the value of accepted amenities/services authorised by the Commissioner for Labour; retain permission, acceptance and valuation evidence. Payroll caps accommodation plus amenities/services at a quarter of salary for the salary period.

name: Registered co-operative dues
authority: EA ss.27(1)(j),32(1): payment to a registered co-operative society with the employee written consent is outside the aggregate 50% limit. Input amount and evidence identify the consented subscription, entrance fee, loan instalment, interest or other due. This is not an employer loan.

name: Commissioner-approved damage recovery
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.29(1): the quarter-month limit may be exceeded with the Commissioner permission. Input amount must be within the evidenced actual loss and the permission, following an inquiry and opportunity to explain; attach that permission to this one-time request. Payroll still enforces the s.32 aggregate salary-period limit except on final salary. https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?WholeDoc=1

name: Ordinary wage backpayment
authority: CPF Board, What payments attract CPF contributions (updated 25 September 2026): wages for employment in one month and contractually payable by the 14th of the following month are Ordinary Wages; wages not meeting both conditions are Additional Wages. The contractual payable date is distinct from the actual payment date. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/what-payments-attract-cpf-contributions

name: Additional wage backpayment
authority: CPF Board, What payments attract CPF contributions (updated 25 September 2026): wages for employment in one month and contractually payable by the 14th of the following month are Ordinary Wages; wages not meeting both conditions are Additional Wages. The contractual payable date is distinct from the actual payment date. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/what-payments-attract-cpf-contributions

name: Prior wage cash repayment
authority: CPF Board refund/adjustment guidance: prior wage repayment and contribution refund or transfer are separate actions. This entry settles evidenced cash only and does not reduce current wage contribution liability. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/compliance-and-rectifications/applying-for-refund-of-cpf-contributions

name: Director fee voted at general meeting
authority: CPF Board director FAQ: directors fees voted at General Meetings do not attract CPF; wages under a separate contract of service remain chargeable. This distinct component excludes the fee from CPF only and preserves the existing SHG/SDL wage assessment pending their own scope. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/are-cpf-contributions-payable-for-directors

name: Permitted recovery of missed employee CPF share
authority: CPF Act s7(6A); Board recovery guidance: employer-error share not recoverable; otherwise Board paid and employee consent forwarded or written Board permission before recovery within six months. Dedicated assessed recovery ledger required.

name: Actual notice breach compensation recovery
authority: Employment Act 1968 s.23(3): actual employee s.11(1) notice liability may be deducted from salary due, subject to a contrary court or Commissioner order. IRAS employment income and personal breach repayment are separate: no reduction of gross taxable wages. Source: https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/monthly-and-daily-salary; https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/termination-of-employment/termination-with-notice; Employment Act 1968 ss.10,11,23(3); https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/part-time-employment/public-holidays
